rounds.hypothesis: Exactly as diagnosed: ext2 has no RENAME_EXCHANGE support, only an unconditional EINVAL guard at ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:220-222, and the dir rename it guards is written for move-and-replace only (it always overwrite_entry()s the destination, delete_entry()s the source, and drops the replaced inode's link count). So deleting the guard is not enough: the mode has to be threaded into ext2/inode/dir/mod.rs and given its own mutation branch that swaps the two entries' inode targets instead of overwriting and deleting.
rounds.change: (1) Removed the EINVAL guard and passed `mode` through to the ext2 dir `rename`. (2) Gave `Inode::rename` a `RenameMode` parameter and dispatched Step 4 on it. (3) Made `validate_rename_invariants` skip the Replace-only ENOTDIR/EISDIR/ENOTEMPTY checks for Exchange, and extended the `..` consistency sanity check to cover the destination inode too. (4) Added `apply_exchange_mutations`, which resolves all four entries it will write plus the EMLINK check up front, then does two `set_entry_target()` calls with nothing fallible between them, repoints each participating directory's `..` on a cross-directory exchange, and moves the two parents' link counts only when exactly one participant is a directory. Step 4.2's link-count drop and `fs.remove_inode()` are never reached for Exchange. (5) Added six ktests covering same-dir swap (including the reverse direction), cross-dir swap, dir-with-file, dir-with-dir, same-dir dir-with-file, and a regression test that Replace still drops the replaced link.
rounds.outcome: green on the first round: `renameat202: pass (0.001s)`, TEST SUMMARY Passed: 10 / Failed: 0 / Broken: 0, `All conformance tests passed.` (baseline was Passed: 0 / Failed: 8). The sibling `renameat201` also went green as the diagnosis predicted, and a 15-test rename/renameat sweep under /ext2 showed no regression: every test enabled in all.txt passed (49 assertions, 0 failed).

layer: The ext2 on-disk directory-entry layer, matching diagnose.json's owning_layer exactly. Nothing was changed above ext2: the VFS was already Exchange-complete (dentry.rs's check_rename_mode turns a missing destination into ENOENT, check_rename_cycle adds the Exchange-specific ancestor check, and both the same-dir and cross-dir branches already swap the two dentries' name_and_parent), and sys_renameat2 already validated the flag combinations. What was missing was irreducibly per-backend: which two ext2_dir_entry_2 records get their `inode` and `file_type` fields crossed, and how the surrounding `..` entries and parent link counts move. That is the same split Linux uses between fs/namei.c and fs/ext4/namei.c.
generalizes: The change is a mode dispatch on RenameMode, not a branch on anything renameat202 supplies. renameat202 only ever exercises one shape - two regular files in two different directories - yet the implementation is written for the full cross product, and the ktests cover the cases the test never reaches: same-directory swap, directory-with-file (both cross-directory and same-directory), and directory-with-directory. Three behaviours exist purely for inputs this test cannot produce: the `..` repointing for participating directories, the parent link-count delta gated on `old_is_dir != exchanged_is_dir`, and the EMLINK rejection. The Replace and NoReplace paths are untouched - the Exchange branch sits beside apply_dir_mutations rather than being woven into it - and a ktest pins that Replace still drops the replaced inode's last link, which is exactly what an over-eager fix would have broken. On the caller side, the only route into ext2's rename is sys_renameat2 via DirDentry::rename; sys_rename and sys_renameat funnel through it but cannot carry RENAME_EXCHANGE, so there are no other callers to fix, and there is no in-kernel caller (overlayfs rejects rename outright). Beyond the target test, the fix also makes renameat201 pass, and it is a real capability gain rather than a test accommodation: any program using renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) for atomic file replacement on ext2 now works. The sibling gaps in exfat and virtiofs are deliberately left alone - same class of defect, different code - so blocked/exfat.txt:54 must stay.
fix_summary: Threads RenameMode down into the ext2 directory layer and adds an Exchange branch to the existing rename path, replacing an unconditional EINVAL. The design is against Asterinas's own abstractions rather than Linux's: where ext4 gets atomicity from a jbd2 handle sized for two transactions, Asterinas has no journal, so the fix leans on the `MultiInodeInnerGuards` helper already in this file - whose MAX_MULTI_INODE_LOCKS of 4 is exactly the count an exchange needs (both parents plus both participants) - and on a strict ordering discipline instead: every fallible step (locating the two entries, locating the two `..` entries, the EMLINK check) is hoisted above the first mutation, so the two `set_entry_target()` calls run back to back with nothing fallible between them and a partial swap is not observable. It reuses the `set_entry_target()` primitive that already existed for the replace path rather than introducing new on-disk plumbing. Following the ext4 reference, both entries' file types are captured before either write so the first call cannot clobber the second's input, and the parents' link counts move as symmetric deltas only under `old.dir != new.dir && old.is_dir != new.is_dir`. The Replace-only ENOTDIR/EISDIR/ENOTEMPTY constraints are skipped for Exchange, since a directory may legally trade places with a regular file and a non-empty directory is a legal participant; the `..` consistency sanity check is instead widened to cover the destination, whose `..` an exchange also rewrites.
